study_type_evidence.quote: Rats received CNP(1-22) or ASB20123 by intravenous (iv) injection into the tail vein or subcutaneous (sc) injection into the back

in_vivo_species.quote: Seven or 8-week-old male SD rats were used.
Sprague Dawley (SD) rats and ICR mice (Charles River Laboratories, Japan) were used in the current study.

agents.name: CNP(1-22) (IV)
agents.sequence_source: Not printed in the body; sequences are PEPlife2's. The body describes ASB20123 as a CNP(1-22) derivative with a C-terminal extension, consistent with the strings.
agents.group_n_quote: Each value represents the mean ± SD of 3 rats.
agents.dose_route_quote: Rats received CNP(1-22) or ASB20123 by intravenous (iv) injection into the tail vein or subcutaneous (sc) injection into the back at a dose volume of 1 mL/kg.
agents.pk_quote: PK parameters were calculated from the individual plasma CNP immunoreactivity-time curves after a single intravenous administration of each peptide in anesthetized rats.

bioanalytical_method: Radioimmunoassay for CNP immunoreactivity using antiserum against the 17-membered internal disulfide ring of CNP and [125I]-[Tyr0]-CNP(1-22) tracer
bioanalytical_quote: CNP immunoreactivity in the plasma was determined by radioimmunoassay (RIA) using antiserum against the 17-membered internal disulfide ring of CNP
notes: All four PEPlife2 values verified against the IV and SC parameter tables: CNP(1-22) 1.42 ± 0.45 min IV and 10.0 ± 5.0 min SC; ASB20123 31.3 ± 4.8 min IV and 32.1 ± 8.0 min SC. PEPlife2 records the last as a bare '32.1', dropping the ±8.0. TWO CORRECTIONS TO PEPlife2 METADATA. (1) The assay is recorded as 'ELISA' but the body says RADIOIMMUNOASSAY, with an antiserum against the CNP disulfide ring and a [125I]-[Tyr0]-CNP(1-22) tracer - an immunoreactivity readout that does not distinguish intact peptide from ring-containing fragments. (2) PEPlife2 records no route, so the IV and SC values for each peptide are indistinguishable in the database; for CNP(1-22) the SC value is 7-fold the IV value, a flip-flop absorption effect rather than a change in clearance. The rats were anaesthetised (pentobarbital, later Inactin) for the whole PK study, which the paper notes but does not control for.
